records.author: Squirrel OS HIPAA Officer
records.body: OCR announced its 55th enforcement action under the HIPAA initiative on August 27, 2026, with penalties ranging from $3,500 to $240,000. The primary cited deficiency across enforcement actions is inadequate risk analysis under 45 CFR 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A). The HIPAA Security Rule overhaul remains proposed (not final as of September 2026), but OCR is already citing proposed standards in resolution agreements, particularly around encryption, multifactor authentication, and access logging. Healthcare organizations should ensure their risk analysis is comprehensive, documented, and updated annually at minimum. Squirrel OS mitigations: PQC encryption (Kyber-1024) exceeds current AES-256 requirements; tenantGuard enforces minimum-necessary access; eventSigner provides cryptographic audit trail signing; Constitution Sentinel enforces human-in-the-loop for critical operations. Gaps: FIPS 140-3 validation, BAA documentation. This article is operational guidance, not legal advice.
records.title: OCR 2026 Enforcement Trends — Risk Analysis Focus

records.author: Squirrel OS HIPAA Officer
records.body: The September 14, 2026 audit found no confirmed breach, but ePHI processing must be gated until three controls are closed: quarantine health-adjacent labels from general telemetry; document full encryption and key-lifecycle coverage because reported PQC readiness is 98%; and verify executed BAAs plus subcontractor flow-downs for every processor that could handle ePHI. Maintain a four-factor breach assessment record under 45 CFR 164.400-414 and apply minimum necessary access under 45 CFR 164.502(b). This article is operational guidance, not legal advice.
records.title: Weekly HIPAA Audit Control Gaps — BAA, PQC Evidence, and Health-Adjacent Data

records.author: Gabriel (guardian)
records.body: Identity is the new perimeter — the password is no longer the wall, the MFA prompt is. Minimum bar for any SMB: MFA on every account (Microsoft Authenticator or number-matching, not SMS where avoidable), no shared admin accounts, and least-privilege role assignment — people get the smallest role that lets them work, audited against the principle that a Global Admin list should be short. Conditional access adds judgment: block legacy authentication outright, require compliant devices for admins, and geo-fence where the business genuinely has no traffic. Offboarding is where identity programs die — a named checklist with license reallocation, MFA device cleanup, and mailbox handover, executed the same day. SQUIRL OS mapping: this operation ran a 'clean 10' least-privilege pass on its own tenant (a documented milestone) and operates least-privilege everywhere — SharePoint writes are restricted by design, tenant data is scoped by customer, and no agent gets blanket authority. Practice what you sell.
records.title: Identity & Access — MFA, Conditional Access, and Least Privilege for SMBs

records.author: Gabriel (guardian)
records.body: SMBs bleed money through unmanaged vendor relationships: auto-renewals nobody remembers, overlapping tools (two backup products, three chat apps), and licenses tied to departed employees. Managed IT discipline: keep a vendor register (product, owner, cost, renewal date, notice period, contact), review it quarterly, cancel overlaps deliberately instead of by panic, and negotiate renewals before the auto-renew window closes. The renewal-notice field is the one most people skip — miss it and you're locked in for another year. SQUIRL OS mapping: VendorContract tracks contract_id, value, auto_renew, renewal_notice_days, and service level; the bill-watch sweep reads it. Lived example from this operation: OpenRouter balance flagged at $0.00 with renewal funding pending — caught by monitoring the vendor layer, not the app layer. Rule of thumb: every recurring dollar needs an owner and a review date.
records.title: Vendor & SaaS Management — Renewals, Contracts, and License Sprawl

records.author: Gabriel (guardian)
records.body: A help desk that can't be measured can't improve. The metrics that matter: first response time (the promise to the customer — silence is the killer), resolution rate and time by category, SLA compliance against the published promise, escalation ratio (too high = automation too timid; zero = automation too bold), first-contact resolution (the gold standard for simple issues), and cost per ticket over time — the curve that proves the 'self-leveling' claim: as the knowledge base grows and matching goes deterministic, cost per incident falls toward a floor, not to zero (novelty stays probabilistic; hardware doesn't self-heal — scope the claim honestly). SLA definition is a contract with reality: same-business-day response backed by real monitoring intervals, not marketing optimism. SQUIRL OS mapping: every number here is already a tracked entity (SLAPolicy, LearningMetric, HealingEventLog with duration/credits) — the platform's proof is that the ledger publishes the actual numbers, including its own mistakes and manual interventions.
records.title: Support Metrics & SLAs — What to Measure and What to Promise

records.author: Gabriel (guardian)
records.body: Microsoft sells SMB plans mostly through four tiers: Business Basic (web apps + email, cheapest), Business Standard (adds desktop Office apps), Business Premium (adds Intune device management + Defender for Business), and the E/A series (enterprise features, compliance, advanced security). Choosing right is about matching features to need, not buying the top tier: most 10-50 seat companies are best served by Basic or Standard, with Premium for regulated or device-heavy environments. Audit the plan mix quarterly — mixed seating wastes money when power users hold premium licenses they never use. SQUIRL OS mapping: licensing is a runtime dependency, not just a cost line — Graph API behavior changes with tier (lived example: a 403 on an API call traced to the app registration missing the right license tier, fixed by gate-checking the license before blaming the code). License assignment and reallocation also ride the onboarding/offboarding checklist (KB-MIT-011).
records.title: Microsoft 365 Business Plans & Licensing — Choosing and Auditing the Right Tier

records.author: Gabriel (guardian)
records.body: If your email doesn't arrive, nothing else you do matters. Three DNS records decide deliverability: SPF (which servers may send as your domain), DKIM (cryptographic signature proving the message wasn't altered), and DMARC (policy telling receivers what to do with failures — monitor, quarantine, reject). Setup order matters: SPF first, then DKIM, then DMARC in monitor mode, tightening after a few weeks of clean reports. Common failures: DKIM CNAME records not added after domain verification (mail signs with onmicrosoft.com fallback — degrades deliverability), SPF exceeding the 10-DNS-lookup limit, and DMARC published at p=none forever. SQUIRL OS mapping: this operation lived a real DKIM CnameMissing repair in its own tenant — the fix is a documented playbook (verify domain, publish the two CNAMEs, wait for propagation, confirm selectors signing). Email monitoring then covers the inbound side: phishing, spoofing of your own domain, and quarantine review.
records.title: Email Deliverability & Security — SPF, DKIM, DMARC in Practice

records.author: Gabriel (guardian)
records.body: Every ticket walks the same road: intake (a channel — email, portal, chat — turns a human problem into a record), triage (category, priority, severity, and who owns it), diagnosis (what is actually wrong vs. what was reported), resolution (the fix, applied and verified — an unverified fix is a rumor), and closure (the client confirms, the record captures what happened and what was learned). Two rules make the difference between a help desk and a noise factory: never resolve without verification, and never close without writing down what you learned — the next ticket on the same problem should start smarter. Priority is about business impact, not who shouts loudest: P1 is 'the business is bleeding,' P3 is 'one person is annoyed.' SQUIRL OS mapping: ServiceTicket + the Tecnichain queue implement this lifecycle; verification is a first-class playbook phase, and every healing event writes a learning record (Pattern + LearningMetric) — the self-leveling loop is this discipline executed by machine.
records.title: The Help Desk Ticket Lifecycle — Intake to Closure

records.author: Gabriel (guardian)
records.body: Automation scales a help desk; judgment keeps it honest. The working pattern: deterministic, well-understood fixes run automatically (password resets, service restarts, known-good playbook steps); anything probabilistic gets confidence-gated — the system proposes, and a human confirms; and anything critical, financial, or evidence-sensitive escalates to a person by default, no exceptions. The same logic gates what an AI support bot may do: it answers from a knowledge base, executes bounded playbook actions, and hands off cleanly to a human when confidence drops or stakes rise. The bot must never fake a fix, never improvise outside its playbooks, and never ask the end user to approve something the user can't evaluate — the end user is the audience, not the approver; human-in-the-loop means the operator/admin side, not the frightened customer. SQUIRL OS mapping: this is literally the platform's operating doctrine (confidence-gated healing, constitutional governance, end-user-as-observer) — the help desk product is the doctrine with a friendly face.
records.title: Automation & AI in the Help Desk — Where Machines End and Humans Begin

records.author: Gabriel (guardian)
records.body: Managed devices are the difference between 'we think the laptop is fine' and 'we know it is.' Microsoft's SMB path is Intune for enrollment and configuration plus Defender for Business for threat protection: enrollment ties a device to the tenant, policy pushes encryption, patch, and baseline settings, and Defender reports detections to a console instead of to nobody. What to enforce at minimum: disk encryption (BitLocker), OS patch currency, Defender on and updated, screen-lock, and a wipe path for lost devices. Companies with BYOD mixtures should split policy: compliant-owned devices get full policy, personal devices get app-protection (containerized corporate data) rather than full control — it keeps employees from revolting. SQUIRL OS mapping: device posture is a first-class monitored layer in the platform adapters (Windows Intune/Defender, macOS Jamf/Keychain, iOS APNs) — enrollment status and Defender signal loss are anomaly classes with playbooks, because an unmanaged endpoint silently breaks everything else on this page.
records.title: Device Management — Intune, Defender, and What 'Managed' Means

records.author: Gabriel (guardian)
records.body: A Microsoft 365 tenant is the organization's root container: tenant-name.onmicrosoft.com (plus vanity domains), inside which live users, groups, licenses, and services. The Microsoft 365 admin center (admin.microsoft.com) handles business settings — billing, licenses, health status, users; the Entra admin center (entra.microsoft.com) handles identity — users, groups, roles, conditional access. Key concepts every admin must know: admin roles follow least privilege (Global Admin is a last resort, not a default), groups come in three kinds (security, Microsoft 365, mail-enabled), and the service health page is the first place to check before diagnosing 'outage' reports. SQUIRL OS mapping: this operation runs a live tenant (squirlos.onmicrosoft.com with vanity domain mapping), and the Graph 401/403 playbook family exists because license tiers and role assignments gate API behavior — a 403 usually means the app lacks a license, a role, or an admin consent, not that the code is wrong.
records.title: Microsoft 365 Administration Fundamentals — Tenant, Admin Center, Entra ID

records.author: Gabriel (guardian)
records.body: Every small business runs on the same five layers: identity (who can log in), devices (laptops, phones, tablets), network & internet (router, DNS, firewall), cloud services (Microsoft 365, line-of-business apps), and data (documents, mailboxes, financial records). Managed IT is the discipline of keeping all five healthy at once. Common SMB failure points: one shared admin password, no MFA, unmanaged backups, expiring certificates nobody owns, and licenses paid for people who left. A provider's first month is usually an inventory and cleanup pass: enumerate every asset, owner, license, and renewal date, then set a baseline. SQUIRL OS mapping: AssetRecord, VendorContract, Employee, and BackupStatus entities model exactly these layers, and the entity inventory is what the health manifest audits against. Lesson from lived operation: the ledger is only as good as the inventory under it.
records.title: The Small-Business IT Stack — Identity, Devices, Network, Cloud, Data

records.author: Gabriel (guardian)
records.body: Managed IT means an IT service provider (MSP) takes continuous responsibility for a client's technology under a recurring agreement, instead of charging per incident ('break-fix'). Core elements: flat per-user or per-device monthly pricing, a service-level agreement (SLA) defining response and resolution commitments, proactive monitoring rather than waiting for failures, and documented scope (what is covered and what is not). The economic logic for small businesses: predictable monthly cost, fewer catastrophic outages, and no need to hire a full-time IT staff. SQUIRL OS mapping: this is the commercial shape the platform is built for — continuous monitoring (heartbeats), playbook-driven response, and a public ledger of what was done and when. The value claim is 'self-leveling': cost per incident falls over time as the system learns each environment. Compliance: prototype disclaimer applies to all buyer deployments.
records.title: What Managed IT Services Actually Are (MSP Fundamentals)

records.author: Gabriel (guardian)
records.body: RMM is the MSP's nervous system: a lightweight agent (or, in modern architectures, an API integration) reports health metrics from every managed device and service to a central console. The console watches thresholds — CPU, disk, uptime, backup status, mail flow — and raises alerts when something drifts. Good RMM practice: alert on symptoms the client feels, triage the rest quietly, and automate the boring remediations (disk cleanup, service restart, certificate renewal) so humans only see what needs judgment. SQUIRL OS mapping: heartbeat monitoring is the direct analog — each app instance self-reports on schedule, a missed heartbeat is itself an anomaly, and matching + healing happen automatically below the alert line. The difference between us and a classic RMM: ours heals from playbooks and writes a learning record for every fix instead of paging a human for everything.
records.title: Remote Monitoring & Management (RMM) — How Providers Watch Everything

records.author: Gabriel (Guardian) — distilled from public supply-chain security guidance (SLSA/artifact-integrity patterns), not verbatim source text
records.body:
SYMPTOMS -> ACTIONS:
- Package hash mismatch, unexpected version bumps, build integrity failure, artifact-feed anomalies -> classify supply_chain_compromise (or supply_chain_cascade variant)
ISOLATE: freeze deployments; circuit-break the artifact feed; isolate affected pipeline runners.
HEAL: pin known-good versions; re-verify all signatures (PQC where applicable); rebuild from clean base image.
VERIFY: artifact chain re-validated end-to-end; zero unsigned code paths; hashes match registry.
TIE-IN: healing_tool_dependency_poison is the internal-runtime cousin of this class — same containment shape.
records.title: Supply Chain / Dependency Compromise — Isolation Matrix

records.author: Gabriel (Guardian) — distilled from public guidance (CISA/NIST incident patterns), not verbatim source text
records.body:
SYMPTOMS -> ACTIONS:
- Mass file-encryption signatures on one host then neighbors (SMB fan-out) -> classify ransomware_lateral_movement, severity critical
- Encryption-typed I/O burst on EDR alert -> ISOLATE IMMEDIATELY: network-isolate host, revoke all active sessions + refresh tokens, disable implicated accounts
- Propagation via valid credentials (hop 2 shows no malware) -> revoke ALL account sessions domain-wide, rotate secrets
HEAL: quarantine binaries; restore from immutable backup; re-issue keys with approved PQC algorithms only (CRYSTALS-Dilithium3, Kyber-1024, SPHINCS+-256f) — NEVER RSA fallback.
VERIFY: two consecutive clean heartbeats, zero encryption signatures, EDR sweep clean, credentials fully rotated.
HUMAN GATE: in a fintech transaction flow -> PredictiveAlert + Leon ACK before healing executes (Rule 2). Two failed heal attempts -> escalate immediately (Rule 9).
records.title: Ransomware & Lateral Movement — Containment Matrix

records.author: Gabriel (Guardian) — distilled from public DDoS mitigation guidance (edge/provider patterns), not verbatim source text
records.body:
SYMPTOMS -> ACTIONS:
- Request volume >> baseline (N-sigma), origin latency climbing, 5xx at edge -> classify massive_ddos, severity high/critical by saturation
ISOLATE: edge rate-limiting; circuit-break the saturated route; ASN/geo heuristic filtering; cache-only serving mode; upstream provider escalation (they own the pipes).
HEAL: shift traffic to secondary edge; re-warm caches; progressively lift filters as volume subsides.
VERIFY: origin latency normal, legitimate-traffic ratio restored across 2 consecutive cycles.
NOTE: the fix lives at the EDGE and the PROVIDER. The runtime's job is fast classification + circuit-breaker trips, not fighting the flood at origin.
records.title: Volumetric DDoS / Edge Saturation — Mitigation Matrix

records.author: Gabriel (Guardian) — distilled from public guidance (NIST SP 800-61 incident-handling patterns), not verbatim source text
records.body:
SYMPTOMS -> ACTIONS:
- Bulk deletes, mass permission changes, off-hours admin activity, dormant-account-then-burst pattern -> classify insider_threat_wipeout, severity critical
CARDINAL RULE: EVIDENCE FIRST — take a signed forensic snapshot BEFORE any rollback. Auditability before recovery; hasty auto-remediation destroys the evidence trail.
ISOLATE: suspend account, revoke sessions, block outbound exfiltration channels, freeze linked automation tokens.
HEAL: restore destroyed state from backup; rotate EVERY secret the account could reach; recertify sibling privileged accounts.
VERIFY: destructive-action log complete and signed; no orphaned grants; audit trail intact.
TIE-IN: this class is why the containment-and-escalate doctrine (KB-SEC-006) exists.
records.title: Insider Threat / Destructive Privileged Action — Response Matrix

records.author: Gabriel (Guardian) — distilled from public IAM hardening guidance (least-privilege/JIT patterns), not verbatim source text
records.body:
SYMPTOMS -> ACTIONS:
- Impossible-travel logins, dormant-account activation, privilege-use bursts, standing broad roles -> classify privileged_account_anomaly
ISOLATE: enforce step-up authentication; revoke flagged sessions.
HEAL: eliminate standing privileges -> just-in-time elevation; rotate credentials; re-enroll PQC keys; quarantine unused admin accounts.
VERIFY: privilege audit shows zero standing-broad roles; anomaly does not recur next cycle.
PATTERN: least-privilege is the PERMANENT fix — every privileged-account anomaly is a standing-privilege finding in disguise.
records.title: Privileged Account Anomaly — IAM Remediation Matrix

records.author: Gabriel (Guardian) — SQUIRL OS original doctrine, ratified by Leon (Sprint 1, Sept 11, 2026)
records.body:
PURPOSE: define what software CAN and CANNOT heal. Honest classification beats fake repair.
UNHEALABLE CLASSES (contain + escalate ONLY): physical/facility disasters (fire suppression, data center fire/flood, power grid failure, physical HVAC), hardware loss, early-stage active attacks where automated action risks destroying forensic evidence, anything requiring physical presence.
DOCTRINE: (1) contain blast radius; (2) signed evidence snapshot; (3) critical PredictiveAlert to the human; (4) NEVER auto-remediate these classes; (5) log as 'contained' — NOT counted as healing misses.
WHY IT MATTERS: counting a burning building as a healing miss is a category error. From Sprint 1 forward, benchmarks report TWO ratios with full disclosure: RAW auto-heal ratio (definition unchanged, for honest trend continuity) and HEALABLE-CLASS ratio (unhealable classes excluded, denominator change disclosed). Deterministic honesty: never hide a denominator change, always print both.
records.title: Containment-and-Escalate Doctrine — Unhealable Classes

records.author: Gabriel (guardian ingest) — authorized by Leon, Sept 10 2026; distilled from public Microsoft troubleshooting patterns + LIVE tenant repair (DKIM CnameMissing fix, Sept 8 2026)
records.body: Email auth stack. SPF: TXT at root, include chain HARD LIMIT 10 DNS lookups (over-limit = permerror for everything downstream); consolidate includes, use ?all softfail deliberately. DKIM: enable per-domain in Defender; requires TWO selector CNAMEs (selector1._domainkey / selector2._domainkey) pointing at the EXACT target from Microsoft's own dialog (lived: CnameMissing Client Error until both were published in Wix DNS; the '.com' in the target stays). Propagation minutes-to-4-days; use Rotate DKIM keys after CNAMEs resolve; re-toggle signing after. DMARC: policy at _dmarc.domain (p=none/quarantine/reject, pct ramp, rua= for reports); alignment relaxed vs strict — DKIM d= must align with From: domain. Verification is ALWAYS the message header: Authentication-Results showing spf=pass, dkim=pass, dmarc=pass.
records.title: SPF/DKIM/DMARC — Record Formats, Failure Modes & the Propagation Trap

records.author: Gabriel (guardian ingest) — authorized by Leon, Sept 10 2026; distilled from public Microsoft troubleshooting patterns
records.body: Endpoint layer. INTUNE ENROLLMENT: error-code first (catalog families: cert/NDES expiry, licensing, endpoint reachability, quota) — enrollment endpoints (enrollment.manage.microsoft.com, *.manage.microsoft.com) must be network-reachable; ghost device records cause hard-stuck retries → clean the record, re-enroll. COMPLIANCE drift: force re-evaluation then reassign policy; check device check-in schedule. DEFENDER: alert triage = evidence chain first (process tree, file hash, user context) — true positive → contain/isolate device, remove persistence, rotate creds; false positive → narrowest exclusion with documented justification, never rule suppression. Sensor health: agent version, connectivity, tamper protection. ASR rules: expect initial friction, tune by documented exclusions. Never auto-remediate an endpoint without a logged disposition reason — triage quality IS the product here.
records.title: Intune & Defender — Enrollment, Compliance & Alert Triage Patterns

records.author: Gabriel (guardian ingest) — authorized by Leon, Sept 10 2026; distilled from public Microsoft troubleshooting patterns + live tenant repairs, NOT verbatim Microsoft content
records.body: Master map for M365 tenant repair. Failure classes by service: ENTRA ID — CA policy drift (KB-MSFT-002), sync failures (005), Graph 401/403 (006), MFA registration gaps (PB-M365-MFA-REG). EXCHANGE ONLINE — NDR matrix (003), email auth SPF/DKIM/DMARC (004), mail flow. SHAREPOINT/ONEDRIVE — sync failures, permissions, list thresholds (008). INTUNE/DEFENDER — enrollment, compliance, alert triage, sensors (007). LICENSING — group-based errors, seat math (009). SERVICE HEALTH — Microsoft-side vs tenant-side triage (009). Each class maps to a PB-M365 playbook in the M365 Tenant Repair Series v1. Rule of the corpus: fix by class, verify by Graph GET, log as healing event — no freehand tenant surgery.
records.title: M365 Troubleshooting Matrix — Service Map & Playbook Cross-Reference

records.author: Gabriel (guardian ingest) — authorized by Leon, Sept 10 2026; distilled from public Microsoft troubleshooting patterns
records.body: SharePoint/OneDrive sync triage. Common failure classes: files-need-attention (path length, blocked file types, invalid characters, path >400 chars), permissions (library inheritance broken, per-user deny), quota (site + user), 5000-item list view threshold (index/managed metadata; large-list design), and sync-client cache corruption. Repair ladder: read the sync client error first → fix naming/permissions/quota → unlink/relink the failing library → clear sync cache as last resort (forces full re-download; schedule with the user). Known Folder Move: pre-checks (available disk space, no other redirects, OneDrive signed in) then run, never force during user session. Deleted personal sites require site re-provision. Verify by file-count reconciliation between source and cloud — green icon alone is not verification.
records.title: SharePoint/OneDrive — Sync Failures, Thresholds & the Repair Ladder

records.author: Gabriel (guardian ingest) — authorized by Leon, Sept 10 2026; distilled from public Microsoft troubleshooting patterns
records.body: Two disciplines in one article. LICENSING: group-based licensing errors — SKU conflict (two plans with overlapping services, only one wins), dependency missing (a SKU that requires another first), usageLocation invalid (assign a location, esp. for plans requiring country), group removal cascades (removing a user from a group de-provisions mid-session). Seat math: Graph subscribedSkus purchased vs assigned vs consuming — drift = billing money leak. SERVICE HEALTH: pull via Graph /admin/serviceAnnouncement (advisories + incidents); ALWAYS separate Microsoft-side from tenant-side before remediating — fixing a Microsoft incident 'locally' wastes the window and corrupts your baselines. Capture tenant impact metrics BEFORE remediation so benchmarks stay honest. Escalate to Microsoft support with correlation IDs when impact persists past the incident ETA.
records.title: Licensing Errors & Service Health — Microsoft-Side vs Tenant-Side Triage

records.author: Gabriel (guardian ingest) — authorized by Leon, Sept 10 2026
records.body: The M365 Tenant Repair Series v1 playbook map. DKIM (dkim_validation_failure → PB-M365-DKIM-001, confidence .85). CA baseline drift (conditional_access_baseline_drift → PB-M365-CA-BASELINE-002, .95 — deterministic count check, 3 lived successes). Mail flow NDR (mail_flow_delivery_failure → PB-M365-MAILFLOW-001, .80). Email auth (email_auth_spf_dmarc_failure → PB-M365-SPF-DMARC-001, .80). Entra sync (entra_sync_failure → PB-M365-ENTRA-SYNC-001, .80). Intune (intune_enrollment_failure → PB-M365-INTUNE-001, .75). Defender (defender_alert_triage → PB-M365-DEFENDER-001, .75). OneDrive (onedrive_sync_failure → PB-M365-ONEDRIVE-001, .75). Licensing (license_assignment_failure → PB-M365-LICENSE-001, .85). Graph API (graph_api_permission_failure → PB-M365-GRAPH-001, .90 — 3 lived successes). Service health (service_health_degradation → PB-M365-SVCHEALTH-001, .90). MFA reg gap (mfa_registration_gap → PB-M365-MFA-REG-001, .80). GATING RULE: below-confidence detections stay 'detected' + PredictiveAlert (never auto-heal low confidence); fintech/settlement-touching flows are ALWAYS human-in-loop regardless of confidence (core directive 2); playbook steps are immutable at runtime — new steps go through SIP → approval → redeploy (core directive 10).
records.title: M365 Tenant Repair Series v1 — Playbook Map & Gating Rules

records.author: Gabriel (guardian ingest) — authorized by Leon, Sept 10 2026; distilled from public Microsoft troubleshooting patterns
records.body: NDR triage matrix. 5.1.x recipient-side: mailbox missing/disabled, address typo, address book policy mismatch → provision/alias or fix rule. 5.4.x routing: DNS misconfiguration, connector loops, transport rule loops → fix connectors/rules; check MX points to the right tenant (msub- records for EOP). 5.7.x policy/auth: SPF/DKIM/DMARC failure, connector TLS failure, tenant restriction or spam policy block → fix email auth (KB-MSFT-004), check TLS settings, review Defender action center for tenant blocks. Always run message trace FIRST for the event timeline before touching config. Deferred-delivery vs bounced: queue depth matters. Fintech caveat: settlement-related mail flows are critical-severity — human-in-loop before any healing action (core directive 2).
records.title: Exchange Online Mail Flow — NDR Classification & Repair Matrix

records.author: Gabriel (guardian ingest) — authorized by Leon, Sept 10 2026; distilled from public Microsoft troubleshooting patterns
records.body: Identity sync triage. Entra Connect/Cloud Sync health: connector status + last sync vs interval; export errors block write-back. DuplicateAttributeResiliency errors: UPN and proxyAddresses are the two big ones — fix the ON-PREM source to a unique value, never edit the cloud object to mask a conflict (it re-conflicts next sync). Soft vs hard match: match on proxyAddresses/UPN first, then sourceAnchor — a bad soft match merges the wrong objects (worst failure class; requires cleanup, not patching). Deleted users: soft-delete restore window 30d. Check service account expiry — stale connector credentials produce silent sync stoppage. Rule: identity objects are the substrate of every other service — a sync anomaly is ALWAYS investigated before downstream symptoms (mail, licensing, Intune) are patched.
records.title: Entra ID Sync — Duplicate Attributes, Soft Matches & Silent Stoppage

records.author: Gabriel (guardian ingest) — authorized by Leon, Sept 10 2026; distilled from public Microsoft troubleshooting patterns + live tenant repairs
records.body: CA not applying to a user: check (1) policy state — report-only does not enforce; (2) user/group exclusions; (3) policy applicability conditions (platform, location, risk); (4) sign-in logs show which policies applied and why not. SECURITY DEFAULTS vs CA are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE at enforcement (lived: HTTP 400 'must disable Security defaults before enabling a Conditional Access policy', TKT-M365-005) — report-only coexists fine; Security Defaults ON does provide baseline MFA + legacy-auth block, so a 0-CA finding may be less severe than it first reads. MFA loop: persistent browser session, sign-in frequency, remembered devices (MFA throttle defaults ~30d). CA requires at least Entra P1 (bundled in Business Premium). Baseline doctrine (PAT-M365-CA-BASELINE): 3 policies (BLOCK-LEGACY-AUTH, MFA-ALL-USERS, MFA-ADMINS) — expected missing on EVERY new tenant; auto-healable, report-only first, fetch role template IDs at runtime.
records.title: Conditional Access Troubleshooting — Policy Drift, MFA Loops, Security Defaults

records.author: Gabriel (guardian ingest) — authorized by Leon, Sept 10 2026; distilled from public Microsoft troubleshooting patterns + LIVE tenant repairs (3 lived Graph failures: TKT-M365-004/005, TKT-EXO-002)
records.body: Graph API failure decoding. 401 = token problem: expired client secret/cert, wrong authority endpoint, clock skew. 403 = authorization problem, three sub-classes: (1) missing APP permission — the scope was never added; (2) missing ADMIN CONSENT — added but not granted (check the API permissions blade status column); (3) LICENSE-TIER GATE — the operation requires a higher license (lived: IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All returns 403 on Business Premium because risk detection needs Entra ID P2, TKT-M365-004; this is a capability boundary, NOT a misconfiguration — document it, never retry-grant). Least-privilege doctrine (lived: clean-10 token, HE-M365-CA-002): grant READ where read suffices (Mail.Read over Mail.ReadWrite — TKT-EXO-002 doctrine), revoke everything unused, verify the token = exactly the intended role set. App-only vs delegated: service automation runs app-only.
records.title: Graph API 401/403 — Permission Drift, Consent Gaps & License-Tier Gates

records.author: Gabriel (guardian ingest) — authorized by Leon, Sept 10 2026
records.body: Hamiltonian mechanics describes system evolution by H(q, p) — total energy as a function of position and momentum; Hamilton's equations evolve state through phase space. Liouville's theorem: Hamiltonian flow preserves phase-space volume — information is not created or destroyed, only redistributed; the mathematical ancestor of 'no silent state drift' in Squirrel OS (every state transition logged, signed, verifiable). Noether's theorem: every continuous symmetry corresponds to a conserved quantity — governance invariants are conserved quantities. records.author: Gabriel (Squirrel OS)
records.body: Privacy and data protection compliance for Squirrel OS Technologies. APPLICABLE LAWS: (1) GDPR (EU) — lawful basis Art. 6, data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure, portability, restriction, objection), DPA requirements, SCCs for international transfers, DPIA for high-risk processing, 72-hour breach notification. Maximum fine: 4% of annual global turnover or EUR 20M. (2) CCPA/CPRA (California) — consumer rights: know, delete, correct, opt-out of sale/sharing. 'Do Not Sell or Share' link required on website. Applies to businesses with >$25M revenue, >100K consumers, or 50%+ revenue from selling data. (3) TDPSA (Texas) — effective Jul 1, 2024. Consumer rights: access, correct, delete, opt-out of sale. Applies to businesses conducting business in Texas with >$25M revenue or processing data of >50K Texas residents. No private right of action (AG enforcement only). (4) Colorado Privacy Act, Virginia CDPA, Utah UCPA, Connecticut CTDPA — similar to CCPA with variations. 5+ additional states enacting in 2026-2027. COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS: Privacy policy covering all applicable laws, data mapping/inventory, retention schedules, breach notification procedures (state-by-state timing), cookie consent mechanism, data processing addendum (DPA) template for customers, vendor DPAs, records of processing activities (GDPR Art. 30). BREACH NOTIFICATION: Texas — notify affected individuals without unreasonable delay (Tex. Bus. & Com. Code Sec. 521.053). California — specific content requirements, 72-hour timeline for regulated entities. All 50 states have breach notification laws with varying requirements. SQUIRREL OS SPECIFIC: System processes operational data (anomalies, health metrics, playbooks). No PII stored in healing logs per Rule #8 (redact all sensitive data). Customer data isolated per tenant isolation policy. PQC encryption (Kyber-1024) for data at rest and in transit.

records.author: Gabriel (Squirrel OS)
records.body: Tax optimization strategies for SquirlOS Technologies LLC (Texas single-member LLC). 1. INCOME SPLITTING: Consider S-Corp election (Form 2553) once net income exceeds ~$80K — splits income between salary (subject to FICA) and distributions (not subject to SE tax). Saves ~15.3% on distribution portion. 2. HOME OFFICE DEDUCTION: Simplified method $5/sqft up to 300 sqft = $1,500/yr max, or actual expenses (mortgage interest, utilities, insurance pro-rated by sqft). 3. RETIREMENT: Solo 401(k) — contribute up to $23,000 (2026) as employee + up to 25% of net self-employment income as employer. Total limit ~$69,000. Reduces taxable income. 4. R&D CREDIT: IRC Section 41 — Squirrel OS development qualifies. 20% credit on qualified research expenses above base amount. 5. QBI DEDUCTION: Section 199A — 20% deduction on qualified business income for pass-through entities (through 2025, pending extension). 6. IP HOLDING COMPANY: Consider separate IP holding entity for patent licensing — royalty income may qualify for lower tax rates. Consult attorney for trust/LLC structure. 7. VEHICLE DEDUCTION: Section 179 or actual costs + mileage (2026 standard rate ~$0.67/mile). 8. EDUCATION DEDUCTION: Continuing education, professional development, certifications related to business. ALWAYS cite IRC section and IRS publication for each strategy.

records.body: Trust and entity structuring guide for Squirrel OS Technologies. CURRENT STRUCTURE: SquirlOS Technologies LLC (Texas single-member LLC). Leon Calvin Long II is sole owner. 8 patents pending + 5 SBIR tracks. RECOMMENDED STRUCTURE (consult attorney): (1) IP HOLDING TRUST — transfer patent ownership to irrevocable trust for asset protection and estate planning. Trust licenses patents to LLC for commercialization. (2) OPERATING LLC — SquirlOS Technologies LLC continues as operating entity, receives patent license from trust. (3) ROYALTY FLOW — LLC pays royalty to trust (deductible business expense for LLC, income for trust at potentially lower tax rate). BENEFITS: Asset protection (patents shielded from LLC creditors), estate planning (trust beneficiaries), tax optimization (royalty payments reduce LLC taxable income). COMPLIANCE: Trust needs separate EIN, annual trust tax return (Form 1041), K-1 to beneficiary. Patent assignments recorded with USPTO. CRITICAL: Attorney must explicitly separate pre-existing IP from any work-for-hire (Bosch startup context). Leon retains sole ownership of all patents. Patent license terms must be arms-length.
records.title: Trust & Entity Structuring — IP Holding Trust + Operating LLC
